Lessons.Title: Sums and Differences of Fractions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will consider strategies for adding and subtracting fractions with the same denominator, including mixed numbers, and to recognize when it is helpful to decompose numbers or write equivalent fractions when finding sums and differences of fractions.
Key idea: Adding and subtracting mixed and improper fractions calls for flexible decomposition and equivalence.
How to reason: Convert or decompose wholes when subtraction needs regrouping; check unknown addends by inverse operations.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up: Number Talk: Subtract Some Eighths (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

Activity 1: Make It True (20 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\underline{\hspace{0.5in}} + \frac{2}{6} = 1\frac{1}{6}\), \(2\frac{4}{5} + \underline{\hspace{0.5in}} = 7\frac{1}{5}\), \(3 - 2\frac{1}{3} = \underline{\hspace{0.5in}}\), \(4\frac{1}{12} - 2\frac{5}{12} = \underline{\hspace{0.5in}}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 2: To Decompose or Not to Decompose (15 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as \(\frac{18}{5} - \frac{7}{5}\), \(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{9}{6}\), \(7 - 1\frac{3}{8}\), \(\frac{102}{100} + 5\frac{27}{100}\). First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.
Original source Cool-down is access-restricted/unverified; Edulytics substitutes goal-aligned independently authored teacher-reviewed exit prompt.
Edulytics worked model: Evaluate 4 and 1/12 minus 2 and 5/12.. Explain every transformation and check using equal wholes/units.
Open reflection: Original missing-number equations, sorting cards and strategy discussions are teacher reviewed.
